newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks back off fresh highs eyeing Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks back off fresh highs eyeing Wall St.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended firmer on Wednesday, although off an intraday record high, tracking a movement on Wall Street, dealers said.
Ibex resistance at 7,200 proved hard to consolidate and this should continue as a key level for the short term.
Banks were at the centre of attention, with strong prospects for first half results boosting prices.
The general index rose 3.42 points, 0.55 percent, 627.21 and Ibex up 25.61 points, 0.36 percent, to 7,164.71, off a fresh intraday high of 7,222.31.
BBV gained 240 pesetas to 12,880, and dealers forecast it should rise over 13,000 pesetas this year.
With domestic funds still looking to buy, banks stand to gain even after this year's spectacular run, dealers said.
"We're looking at very strong first half earnings for both Santander and BBV, with both up to ten percent below their fair value even at these levels," said a Benito y Monjardin dealer.
Conversely utilities are still weighed down by uncertainties over the deregulation of the market, tariffs and lower rainfall, although Endesa should be bolstered by the autumn public offering.
